answer: Random paid attestation turns every identity claim into a lottery an attacker cannot rig. At unpredictable intervals, a verifier is drawn to stake coins on whether a newcomer is genuine; a wrong call forfeits the stake, a right one earns a fee. Like a sonnet whose rhyme only holds if each line is honest, the check binds the whole identity graph: every vertex that vouches for a fake risks its own stake, and the kernel of trust stays small because faking thousands of identities means funding thousands of losing bets.
